sam: heads-up — importing HF model 'big-optim-v2' ran into a weird discrepancy during conversion. generation diverges ~512 tokens in. Noticed config.json has rope_scaling + sliding_window set and num_key_value_heads=16, but runtime reports num_kv_heads=32 after conversion. anyone seen rope_scaling + sliding_window flip kv heads?

maya: hmm. seen similar when sliding_window interacts with special tokens and tokenizer.model_max_length. sliding_window can shift the effective positions, then our converter tries to pad/duplicate kv heads to match an internal windowing heuristic.

sam: here's the relevant config snippet from HF model:```json
{
  "max_position_embeddings": 4096,
  "num_key_value_heads": 16,
  "rope_scaling": {"type": "linear", "factor": 1.3},
  "sliding_window": true
}
```

sam: converter command I used: `python -m redwood.convert --hf ./checkpoint --output ./rw-model`

eng-bot: conversion-checker: WARNING: rope_scaling present but runtime does not support dynamic rope_scaling patches; falling back to positional rescaling at load time. KV head canonicalization applied -> reported num_kv_heads=32. See /tmp/convert-1859.log

maya: that fallback was the culprit last week. When we fallback we currently mirror attention head grouping to keep shadowed KV caches compatible, which doubles heads for some architectures. It was done to avoid token indexing errors, but it breaks quantized kernels assumptions (4-bit path expects original head count).

sam: ok — two problems then: (1) quantized kernel asserts head count -> crash or slower path, (2) chat templates adding <BOS>/<EOS> cause effective positions to shift during sliding_window, so generation context slices don't align with cached KV windows.

leo: quick checklist: 1) verify tokenizer.special_tokens_map (BOS/EOS) are the same pre/post convert; 2) run `scripts/inspect_pos_mapping.py --model ./rw-model` to compute effective position offsets; 3) try conversion flag `--preserve-num-kv-heads` (internal prototype) to avoid doubling.

maya: repro snippet I used:```bash
# generate 600 tokens and compare logits
python evals/compare_generation.py \
  --model-a ./hf-checkpoint \
  --model-b ./rw-model \
  --prompt-file tests/prompts/long_prompt.txt \
  --max-tokens 600
```

maya: output diff showed token shift exactly at 512 and subsequent tokens are permuted (not just different choices) — consistent with position indexing mismatch.

sam: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/converter/pull/1234 — adds special_tokens normalization, preserves num_key_value_heads when sliding_window=true, and emits a conversion-report that lists any rope_scaling fallback. cc @leo

leo: will review. plan to include a unit that runs a short quantized kernel smoke test against the converted model before publishing to the hosted catalog. ETA: EOD today.

maya: I'll add an eval run to the nightly benchers to look for quality regressions and latency change after we flip preserve-num-kv-heads. Also adding a small patch to the runtime that logs if effective_max_pos != config.max_position_embeddings so we can catch mismatches early. :mag:
